newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss on cult suicide watch, seek curbs on sects.
newsitem.headline: Swiss on cult suicide watch, seek curbs on sects.

text.p: A top Swiss justice official proposed new measures and tighter controls on Thursday to curb activities of deadly cults amid fears that suicides among followers of the Swiss-based Solar Temple are far from over.

Geneva justice chief Gerard Ramseyer told a news conference on the results of a study on cults that curbs on commercial activities of such groups and a police information page on the Internet were among measures being discussed.

Ramseyer said police feared Solar Temple followers, mostly well-off professionals who are taught the world will end in fire and that to reach the afterworld they must die by burning, could attempt mass suicides with the approaching millennium.

"We fear suicides may increase ahead of the year 2000 but we can't stop them. We can't stop people taking their own lives. How can the police intervene?" he asked. "When do we have the legal right to go into people's lives for surveillance?"

A total of 74 followers of the bewildering sect that believes "death voyages" by ritualized suicide leads to rebirth in a place called "Sirius", and their family members have killed themselves since 1994.
The last suicides were in March when five believers, two of them Swiss, killed themselves in Canada.
The cult won international notoriety after mass suicides and murders killed 53 of its members in two Swiss villages in the cantons of Fribourg and Valais and a ski resort in Quebec.

A year later, in December 1995, 16 cult members including several children died in a remote French Alpine forest clearing in a macabre ritual in which most of them were drugged and had plastic bags pulled over their heads before they were shot.
Swiss police have come under fire for not taking action against the surviving cult members. They claim they were blocked by the constitutionally-guaranteed freedom to worship.
Ramseyer said the number of sects in Geneva had jumped to 120 from 80 in January in a sign of increasing activities.
He said Solar Temple had as many as 20 known followers in Geneva and perhaps hundreds in Switzerland and also business activities but it was difficult to keep a tab on them.
"We're lying in constant wait for exact indications of financial activities that could allow us to react. But it's very complicated and mysterious," he said.
Cult-watchers estimate there are thousands of cults spread around the world, with more than 500 in Britain and 2,500 in the United States alone.
